children: Renewable energy, semiconductors and battery storage are expected to attract capital as banks adapt to emerging financing needs

State Bank of India (SBI) Chairman CS Setty has said the next phase of global investment is likely to centre on sunrise sectors such as renewable energy, semiconductors, battery storage, green hydrogen, robotics and biotechnology. He said these industries could attract substantial capital in the coming years, while banks and financial institutions will have to adapt their financing frameworks to support their expansion.

Setty made the remarks at the inauguration of the 13th SBI Banking & Economics Conclave on Wednesday, where he also highlighted the role of India's financial system in supporting technology-driven and sustainability-focused economic growth.

According to Setty, emerging industries are expected to become important destinations for global investment as economies focus increasingly on advanced manufacturing, clean technologies and innovation.
He said India has several factors supporting its participation in this investment cycle, including a skilled workforce, an entrepreneurial ecosystem and expanding technological capabilities.
The focus, however, will need to move beyond developing talent and innovation towards converting these strengths into commercially viable businesses and scalable technologies.

Setty highlighted the need for India to develop enterprises capable of competing in international markets. This would involve strengthening domestic capabilities across manufacturing, technology and intellectual property.
He said the opportunity extends beyond achieving higher economic growth, with greater emphasis required on building businesses that can establish a global presence in emerging industries.

The shift towards frontier technologies is also expected to increase the capital requirements of businesses, particularly in sectors involving large-scale infrastructure, research and development and manufacturing capacity.
The SBI Chairman also pointed to the changing role of banks as India's economy moves towards high-value manufacturing, green technologies and innovation-led businesses.

Technology-intensive and capital-heavy industries can have different funding requirements from traditional businesses. This could require banks and other financial institutions to develop financing structures suited to longer investment cycles and evolving business models.
Setty said the financial sector will have an important role in creating the financing architecture required to support innovation, investment and business expansion.

The transition towards sunrise sectors also raises the importance of connecting economic growth with global competitiveness. For India, this would involve developing the capacity to build and scale enterprises that can compete across international markets.
The sectors identified by Setty span clean energy, advanced technology, life sciences and automation, reflecting the broader shift in global investment towards technology and sustainability.
Conclusion: Setty's remarks underline the changing financing requirements of emerging industries and the role of banks in supporting India's transition towards technology-led and sustainable growth.
